html:
The Battle of Pressburg was fought in July 907 near today's Bratislava, where Magyar horsemen destroyed a Bavarian army sent to drive them out of the Danube basin.

The Magyars had crossed the Carpathians only a few years before, and Great Moravia had fallen to them. The Bavarians hoped to push them back east. Instead their margrave, an archbishop and two bishops died on the field. The defeat closed the east to Frankish expansion for decades and let the Magyars keep raiding Europe until their loss at Lechfeld in 955. It sealed the rule of Hungary over the Slovak lands for the next thousand years.
